Hidden Figures (2016) is an inspiring true story about three extraordinary women—Katherine Johnson, Dorothy Vaughan, and Mary Jackson—whose work at NASA helped make America’s first manned space missions possible. Blending history with heartfelt performances, the film shines a light on the brilliant minds who were overlooked for far too long.

One of the film’s most memorable scenes shows Katherine Johnson running across the NASA campus to use a segregated bathroom. While it powerfully illustrates the discrimination Black women faced at the time, the real story is slightly different. The bathroom incident was actually based on Mary Jackson’s experiences, not Katherine Johnson’s. Johnson later explained that she had unknowingly used the “whites-only” restroom for years because it wasn’t labeled. When someone eventually objected, she simply kept using it—and the issue was quietly dropped.
